articles.title: DPWH blacklists 2 more Discaya firms
articles.summary: The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) has blacklisted two construction firms associated with controversial contractor Sarah Discaya, following contract defaults on projects totaling over…

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) has blacklisted two construction firms associated with controversial contractor Sarah Discaya, following contract defaults on projects totaling over P203 million.

In separate orders issued last week, Pubic Works Secretary Vince Dizon ordered the suspension and blacklisting of YPR General Contractor and Construction Supply Inc., and Way Maker General Contractor OPC from participating in any government bidding activities pursuant to Republic Act 9184 or the Government Procurement Reform Act.

Under Department Order 127, YPR General Contractor was slapped with a two-year suspension for its second offense, following the termination last Oct. 30 of its contract for default on the P95.53-million construction of flood mitigation structures along Aklan River (Package 2) in Kalibo, Aklan.
Meanwhile, Way Maker General received a one-year suspension under Department Order 128 Series of 2026, after defaulting on the P80-million Aklan West Road project that was terminated last Oct. 30.

Way Maker General was hit with another two-year suspension under Department Order 131 for failing to comply with its P28.27-million contract for the establishment of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) facility along Taft Avenue in Ermita, Manila that the DPWH terminated last Nov. 19.

The two firms were among the nine firms revealed to be owned by Discaya during a Senate Blue Ribbon committee hearing last year, where Discaya admitted under oath that she and her family own or hold stakes in nine separate construction companies that actively join DPWH biddings.

During questioning, Discaya confirmed that her network of firms include Alpha and Omega Gen. Contractor & Development Corp., St. Gerrard Construction and Development Corp., St. Timothy Construction Corp., St. Matthew General Contractor and Development Corp., Elite General Contractor and Development Corp., Amethyst Horizon Builders and General Contractor Development Corp., Great Pacific Builders and General Contractor Inc., and YPR and Way Maker One Person Corp.

Discaya initially denied that all nine companies competed against one another for the same contract, but later acknowledged that there were instances where the entities participated in the same bidding process.
DPWH assistant secretaries appointed

Meanwhile, Dizon has appointed two new assistant secretaries at the DPWH, bringing to nine the total number of assistant secretaries at the department, serving under the nine undersecretaries that were created and filled since he assumed leadership of the DPWH in September 2025.

Despite early pledges to streamline operations amid a nationwide “top-to-bottom” cleansing, Dizon had formalized last Sept. 17 a top-heavy administrative structure comprised of nine undersecretaries and assistant secretary assignments.

The latest additions to the central management include Carlo Jauharo Castro – a former public affairs officer of motorcycle ride-hailing app Angkas – as assistant secretary for planning, public-private partnerships, and the National Building Code; and Angelo Nuestro as assistant secretary for information management, a rank downgrade after a stint as undersecretary for connectivity at the Department of Information and Communications Technology in 2022.

They join a crowded pool of assistant secretaries that includes Genevieve Cuaresma (support services), Michelle Mae Vivo (legislative liaison), Melody Anne Calo-Villar (legal service), Michelle de Vera (stakeholders relations and communications), Suzanne Marie Liwanag (Office of the Secretary), and retired Maj. Gen. Rommel Tello (regional operations in Luzon).

Career official Nerie Bueno serves as assistant secretary for regional operations in Visayas and Mindanao, while OIC-Undersecretary Lara Marisse Esquibil is concurrently assistant secretary for external convergence projects.
Directly above the assistant secretaries, a nine-member panel of undersecretaries has been assigned to oversee various specialized services, field operations, and central bureaus.

Senior Undersecretary Emil Sadain retains overall supervision over the five specialized Unified Project Management Office clusters, the RPMO-BARMM, flagship infrastructure projects, and the agency’s management committee.
Regional operations remain split between Undersecretary Arthur Bisnar for Luzon and Undersecretary Ador Canlas for Visayas and Mindanao.

The remaining executive portfolios are distributed among OIC-Undersecretary Lara Marisse Esquibil (technical services and operations), Nicasio Conti (planning), Rio Espiritu (support services), Charles Calima (special concerns), Samuel Rufino Turgano (legal service), and Ricardo Bernabe III, who manages the Office of the Secretary, information management, stakeholders relations and legislative liaison while chairing the human resource selection board.
Under the revised setup, the Internal Audit Service has been placed directly under the supervision and control of the Office of the Secretary.

Critics and agency observers note that while President Marcos ordered a “top to bottom” cleanup of the department following massive flood control project anomalies and budget insertion scandals, Dizon’s response has resulted in a dense top management layer at the DPWH while not cutting posts at the regional and district offices.

articles.title: Impeachment court hopes SC rules soon on vote threshold
articles.summary: To avert a looming constitutional crisis, the Senate impeachment court is counting on the Supreme Court (SC) to swiftly settle the petitions against its decision to count only the votes of present…

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 12:00am
The main building of the Philippine Supreme Court in Manila as taken on Dec. 13, 2024.
Philstar.com / Martin Ramos

MANILA, Philippines — To avert a looming constitutional crisis, the Senate impeachment court is counting on the Supreme Court (SC) to swiftly settle the petitions against its decision to count only the votes of present senators in the two-thirds threshold to convict Vice President Sara Duterte.

Senate impeachment court spokesman Reginald Tongol yesterday said the court anticipated the legal challenges, but stressed that the trial would proceed uninterrupted unless the high court issues a temporary restraining order (TRO).

Recent petitions filed before the SC, including one by former executive secretary Vic Rodriguez, seek a TRO and a writ of preliminary injunction to stop the Senate from applying its new rule, which excludes absent or incapacitated senators from the two-thirds baseline needed for a conviction.
Tongol expressed hope that the SC would hand down its decision while the trial is still ongoing.
“I hope the decision arrives before they (senator-judges) vote on the final question whether to convict or acquit the respondent,” Tongol told radio dzBB.
He warned that resolving the threshold issue after the Senate has already rendered a verdict could lead to massive political instability.

“Of course, we don’t want the impeachment court to have a decision then we’re all left hanging if the respondent will follow it or not because there is a pending issue with the Supreme Court. We don’t want that commotion,” he explained.
SC cases expected

Tongol revealed that presiding officer Francis Escudero fully expected aggrieved parties to elevate the matter to the high court as early as July, deliberately recognizing the threshold debate as a justiciable issue.
Should the SC ask the Senate to comment on the petitions, which allege grave abuse of discretion, Tongol said the chamber is ready to defend its actions.

He argued that the Senate’s decision is “constitutionally bulletproof,” citing the exhaustive due diligence they conducted, which included inviting amici curiae (friends of the court) and holding extensive oral arguments.

articles.title: Chiz clears VP’s AMLC records for impeachment use
articles.summary: Financial documents from the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) can now be used as evidence in the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, following clearance from presiding…

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Financial documents from the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) can now be used as evidence in the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, following clearance from presiding officer Francis Escudero.
Senate impeachment court spokesman Reginald Tongol made the confirmation yesterday, noting that impeachment proceedings are a legal exception to the country’s strict anti-money laundering laws.
“Our presiding officer has already decided to allow those records to be used (as evidence),” Tongol told radio dzBB.
Tongol added that Escudero reviewed the documents and found that their release would not compromise or disclose the AMLC’s confidential investigative methods.
To formally enter the records into the trial, the tribunal would subpoena AMLC executive director Ronald Buenaventura.
He is expected to authenticate the documents and explain the council’s findings to the senator-judges.
The Senate impeachment court is currently on Article II (unexplained wealth). Last week, prosecutors scrutinized Duterte’s alleged business interests, particularly in her hometown in Davao City.

articles.title: No rebranding, hiding system loss charge, Tulfo vows
articles.summary: Consumers will not see the controversial system loss charge simply rebranded and hidden in other sections of their monthly electricity bills as soon as a proposed legislation banning it becomes law,…

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Consumers will not see the controversial system loss charge simply rebranded and hidden in other sections of their monthly electricity bills as soon as a proposed legislation banning it becomes law, Sen. Erwin Tulfo assured the public yesterday.

Addressing fears that power distributors might offset the impending removal of the charge by quietly inflating other fees, Tulfo, chairman of the Senate energy committee, guaranteed that the proposed legislation contains strict safeguards against such practices.
“We have anticipated this loophole and it is unacceptable. We cannot remove systems loss from one line of the electricity bill only to see the same cost transferred somewhere else,” Tulfo said.
The senator sponsored Senate Bill No. 2486, or the proposed Systems Loss Charge Removal Act on the plenary floor last week, certified as a priority measure.
To prevent power companies from circumventing the ban, Tulfo explained that the bill specifically targets the exact billing components that utilities might attempt to exploit.

“This is why the bill we are shepherding now explicitly prohibits distribution utilities and electric cooperative from recovering allowed losses through distribution wheeling charges, supply charges, metering charges, universal charges, subsidies or any other item in the bill,” he noted.
“Why do consumers pay for electricity that they did not consume? Why do consumers bear the brunt of inefficiencies and deteriorating facilities resulting in systems loss?” Tulfo asked.
Pushing for the immediate passage of the measure, the senator emphasized that access to fair utility pricing is essential.
“Electricity is not a luxury. It is a basic necessity the modern society needs to operate with dignity,” Tulfo said.

articles.title: ‘Government to lose P700 million monthly in excise tax suspension’
articles.summary: The government stands to lose at least P700 million a month in revenues after President Marcos suspended the excise tax on liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and kerosene, Customs Commissioner Ariel…

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The government stands to lose at least P700 million a month in revenues after President Marcos suspended the excise tax on liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and kerosene, Customs Commissioner Ariel Nepomuceno said yesterday.

“If we will base it during the previous suspension from April to July, we will also lose a lot. We will lose at least P700 million a month. But we understand, of course, because the times are different now, there are crises. We also need to support our countrymen, especially those who are struggling,” Nepomuceno said.

Finance Secretary Frederick Go, who also sits on the Development Budget Coordination Committee (DBCC), said the resolution is similar to the previous three-month fuel tax relief measure, excluding diesel and gasoline.
Go explained that the covered fuel products are commonly used by vulnerable households for cooking and other daily needs.
“Our consumption of LPG and kerosene is also high. During the suspension (of excise taxes on LPG and kerosene from April to July), the total revenue lost was almost P3 billion,” Nepomuceno said.
He said suspending diesel and gasoline would mean more losses for the government.

“According to the Department of Finance, although suspending the excise tax on gas and diesel will help a lot, the losses would be bigger. That’s probably over P10 billion. That’s why, of course, the DBCC is studying it. It doesn’t seem to be the direction. Because direct assistance through the suspension of LPG and kerosene is more effective,” Nepomuceno added.
He said the BOC will try to find other sources of income to recover the losses from the suspension of excise taxes on LPG and kerosene.
“Our commitment is really to maintain our good collection, and second, we will find ways to increase our revenue collection,” Nepomuceno said.

Business groups and other sectors are asking the government to suspend the bigger 12-percent value-added tax on all petroluem products, warning that soaring fuel prices are passed on to consumers and fuel inflation.

Energy Secretary Sharon Garin certified that the average price of Dubai crude oil in the past month breached the $80-per-barrel threshold, which has been transmitted to the inter-agency DBCC for evaluation.

articles.title: ‘Abolish SK, one youth representative enough’
articles.summary: The Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) should be abolished, election lawyer Romulo Macalintal said, asserting that a single member of the barangay council can represent the youth.

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — The Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) should be abolished, election lawyer Romulo Macalintal said, asserting that a single member of the barangay council can represent the youth.
In an interview with radio dzBB over the weekend, Macalintal said the youngest member of the village council can become chairman of the committee on youth.
Macalintal denounced the postponement of the barangay and SK elections to November 2028 – the third time under the Marcos administration.
The prolonged delay in the BSKE would make incumbent youth council officials ineligible to run in the next elections, he noted.

Provisions of the new law delaying the BSKE, particularly the “fixed” five-year term and the two-year term extension for village and youth council officials, would make SK officials overaged, Macalintal said.
Under the SK Reform Act of 2015, youth council officials must be between 18 to 24 years old at the time of their election.

The SK chairperson would be an ex-officio member of the barangay council and automatically head its youth and sports committee, entitled to a “pro-rata honoraria for every session of the Sangguniang Barangay he or she has attended.”

articles.title: Cardinal backs people’s initiative on anti-dynasty law
articles.summary: Caloocan Bishop Pablo Virgilio David is backing the push for a genuine anti-dynasty law through a people’s initiative.

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 12:00am
Caloocan Bishop Pablo Virgilio Cardinal David
Facebook photo
MANILA, Philippines — Caloocan Bishop Pablo Virgilio David is backing the push for a genuine anti-dynasty law through a people’s initiative.

The “Dapat Isa Lang Movement” launched a signature campaign that aims to gather at least seven million signatures – or 10 percent of the country’s registered voters – to push for a national referendum to enact the law.

“Perhaps this is where we need to rediscover another form of People Power. The Constitution reserves legislative power not only to Congress but also to the people through initiative and referendum,” David said.

Catholic Bishops Conference of the Philippines president and Lipa Archbishop Gilbert Garcera has issued a pastoral statement supporting the Dapat Isa Lang people’s initiative as a peaceful, lawful and democratic means for Filipinos to pursue the long-delayed constitutional mandate.

articles.title: Venezuela releases dozens of political prisoners as election calls grow
articles.summary: A slew of dissidents being released from long-term detention comes days after the nation's interim leader met the US president.

blocks.text: Venezuelan authorities have released a slew of political prisoners, human rights groups say, days after the nation's interim leader met US President Donald Trump in New York.
Among those released in the early hours of Saturday morning was Wilder Vasquez, who was handed a five-year sentence in 2018 over claims he was plotting to kill former President Nicolás Maduro.
Opposition figures have renewed calls for free elections after interim President Delcy Rodriguez held talks with Trump, who captured Maduro earlier this year, at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday.
Her administration previously released hundreds of prisoners as part of a reconciliation effort following Maduro's seizure.
However, these releases slowed to a trickle in April after Rodriguez said the scheme was "coming to an end".
Venezuela's government has not made any statement concerning the latest releases, nor has it indicated whether they were the result of her conversation with the US president.
Gonzalo Himiob, vice-president of rights group Foro Penal, said "a significant number" of political prisoners had been released on Saturday morning from several of Venezuela's detention centres.

Venezuelan Interior Minister Diosdado Cabello, a minister closely associated with Maduro's authoritarian rule, called the interim president's meeting with Trump "a great triumph of the diplomacy of peace".
But opposition voices expressed their disapproval over the meeting, viewing it as a snub of their calls – that the US has previously endorsed – for swift elections.

Pedro Mario Burelli, a former Venezuelan state oil company executive and opposition commentator, called the two world leaders "the shameless puppet and her unscrupulous and undignified puppet-master", adding: "Little has changed in Venezuela under Washington's clumsy and selective oversight."

Venezuela's last elections, held in 2024, in which Maduro was declared the winner, were widely disputed as rigged. Opposition tallies suggested their candidate, who stood after Machado was barred from running, had won by 70% of the vote.

Despite this, the Trump administration backed Rodriguez, Maduro's former vice-president, as his successor rather than opposition leader María Corina Machado after Maduro was seized and put on trial on drug charges in January.
Analysts at the time cast this decision as the US choosing short-term stability in Venezuela until elections could be held.
Rodriguez used her UN General Assembly speech on Thursday to reiterate that there "will be elections in Venezuela", without specifying when.

articles.title: Two people killed as bus crashes on way to Oktoberfest
articles.summary: The bus was traveling from Italy to Munich, carrying 33 Filipino tourists who wanted to visit the famous beer festival. One of the dozens injured remains in life-threatening condition.

image.caption: Emergency services rushed to the scene of the crash in Buchloe, Bavaria near the Austrian border Image: Karl-Josef Hildenbrand/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Two people were killed and many more injured when a bus carrying a group of Filipino tourists overturned in southern Germany on Sunday en route to the Munich Oktoberfest.
The bus was coming from Milan, an Italian city with a large Filipino community.

According to German police, there were 33 tourists on the bus when, at 5:41 a.m. local time (03:41 a.m. GMT), the vehicle went off the side of the A96 highway and overturned. No other vehicles were involved in the crash.

Six of the injured were immediately rushed by helicopter to nearby hospitals, one of whom was thought to still be in a life-threatening condition. Two more were taken by ambulance to the hospital, while another 22 were first treated at the scene before several of those were also brought to the hospital.
Police so far have only identified one of the two people who died as a 58-year-old Filipino citizen.

"It is naturally very chaotic at first, and establishing the facts is difficult,” explained a spokesperson for the local police headquarters. It took police hours to confirm how many people actually were on the bus.
Bus driver charged with negligent homicide

In addition to the 33 tourists, there were the two Italian bus drivers on board, both of whom were not injured in the crash. The driver who was at the wheel at the time of the crash is now being investigated for negligent homicide, police said. "That is standard procedure,” a police spokeswoman explained.

The cause of the accident remained unclear, police said. "The public prosecutor's office has commissioned an accident reconstruction expert report to determine the cause of the crash. It is far too early to comment.”

More than 200 firefighters, medics and police were rushed to the scene of the crash. A section of the highway was completely blocked for some time before, but in the afternoon, traffic was allowed to resume.
There have been a string of bus accidents in recent weeks. Earlier in September, a Dutch coach crashed in Switzerland, killing five, while a bus crash on Germany's A3 highway left 30 people injured.
Oktoberfest draws millions of visitors

Munich’s Oktoberfest is the world’s largest beer festival, attracting millions of visitors to the Bavarian capital each year. Held over roughly two weeks, it combines giant beer tents, traditional Bavarian food, live music and fairground rides, drawing visitors from Germany and around the world.

This year, the Oktoberfest runs from September 19 to October 4. Organizers said that at the halfway point, around 3.8 million people had already visited the festival — about 300,000 more than at the same point last year.

blocks.caption: The Oktoberfest is the world's biggest beer festival and draws millions of international touristsImage: Matthias Schrader/AP Photo/picture alliance

articles.title: PCG deploys aircraft, BRP Teresa Magbanua to locate, challenge China Coast Guard vessel within EEZ
articles.summary: The Philippine Coast Guard has deployed on Sunday an aircraft and a multi-response vessel to locate and challenge a vessel of the China Coast Guard that was monitored to be within the Philippine…

blocks.text: Published September 27, 2026 11:29pm

The Philippine Coast Guard has deployed on Sunday an aircraft and a multi role-response vessel to locate and challenge a vessel of the China Coast Guard that was monitored to be within the Philippine Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), said the PCG in a statement.

Under the directive of Commandant Admiral Ronnie Gil L. Gavan, the PCG aircraft 2081 - a Cessna Grand Caravan - and the BRP Teresa Magbanua (MRRV-9701) were deployed on Sunday, September 27, 2026 to "locate and challenge China Coast Guard vessel CCG-3303."
The China Coast Guard vessel, the PCG said, had been monitored loitering approximately 35 nautical miles northwest of Cabra Island, Occidental Mindoro that is within the EEZ.

The aircraft PCG-2081 took off from Manila for a Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) flight over the said area around 8:40 a.m. and by 9:20 a.m. visually confirmed CCG-3303 at 36.61 nautical miles northwest of Cabra Island.
"PCG-2081 issued multiple radio challenges asserting that the vessel was operating inside the Philippine EEZ without authority. CCG-3303 did not respond to any of the challenges," the PCG said.

On Sunday afternoon, the BRP Teresa Magbanua monitored three People's Liberation Army Navy (PLA-N) warships that were identified with bow numbers 572, 536, and 551. The vessels were operating approximately 31 nautical miles northwest of the island.

"As of this afternoon, MRRV-9701 was shadowing the PLA-N vessels at distances ranging from 0.74 to 6.28 nautical miles while maintaining PCG presence and visibility in the area. This follows the sighting of a PLA-N frigate with bow number 569 approximately 22 nautical miles east-northeast of Bajo de Masinloc on 26 September," the PCG added.

Based on the PCG's assessment, the CCG-3303 and the PLA-N warships may be connected to the Chinese naval shadowing of the ADMM-Plus Experts' Working Group on Maritime Security Joint Cooperative Activity. The said activity in the West Philippine Sea was concluded this week.

"The China Coast Guard's silence in response to PCG radio challenges near Cabra Island mirrors this pattern and strongly suggests that CCG-3303 was operating in support of the PLA-N monitoring effort rather than performing any legitimate coast guard function," the PCG said.

"The PCG reiterates that the waters northwest of Cabra Island lie within the Philippine EEZ, where the Philippines exercises sovereign rights under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) and the 2016 Arbitral Award. The PCG will continue to deploy its air and surface assets to monitor, document, and challenge foreign vessels operating in Philippine waters without authorization," it added.

The PCG also said that the deployment is "in accordance with the guidance of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., who has consistently directed the PCG to maintain presence in strategic locations in the West Philippine Sea and has declared that the Philippines does not intend to yield and that he will not preside over any process that abandons even a square inch of Philippine territory."

"Malacañang has likewise affirmed that government agencies acting in accordance with the law to defend the country's rights and interests in the WPS have the full support of the President," it added. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: ITCZ affects parts of Philippines; Typhoon Queenie exits PAR
articles.summary: The Visayas, Zamboanga Peninsula, Northern Mindanao, Caraga, Lanao del Sur, and Basilan have scattered rain and thunderstorms due to the intertropical convergence zone

blocks.text: QUEENIE. Satellite image of Typhoon Queenie (Surigae) outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility as of September 27, 2026, 8 pm.
PAGASA
The Visayas, Zamboanga Peninsula, Northern Mindanao, Caraga, Lanao del Sur, and Basilan have scattered rain and thunderstorms due to the intertropical convergence zone

MANILA, Philippines – Rain from the intertropical convergence zone (ITCZ) will persist in the Visayas, Mindanao, and Palawan in the next 24 hours, the weather bureau said on Sunday afternoon, September 27.
The ITCZ is a belt near the equator where the trade winds of the Northern Hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere meet.

It is causing scattered rain and thunderstorms in the Visayas, Zamboanga Peninsula, Northern Mindanao, Caraga, Lanao del Sur, and Basilan, as well as isolated rain showers or thunderstorms in the rest of Mindanao and Palawan.
The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said flash floods and landslides are possible.
The rest of Luzon will continue to have generally fair weather, with just localized thunderstorms.
Meanwhile, Typhoon Queenie (Surigae), which did not affect the country, left the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) at 11 am on Sunday.
As of 8 pm, Queenie was already 935 kilometers northeast of extreme Northern Luzon, moving east northeast at 20 kilometers per hour (km/h).
The typhoon’s maximum sustained winds have since reached 175 km/h, with gustiness of up to 215 km/h. Around the time of its exit from PAR, its maximum sustained winds were at 150 km/h.

Queenie entered PAR as a tropical storm last Thursday, September 24, and remained far from Philippine landmass. It intensified into a severe tropical storm on Friday, September 25, and into a typhoon on Saturday, September 26.

Queenie was the Philippines’ 17th tropical cyclone for 2026, and the first for September. As of Sunday evening, no new low pressure areas or potential tropical cyclones are being monitored inside or outside PAR.

For October, November, and December, PAGASA predicted that there could be one or two tropical cyclones per month. The next six local names are Rosal, Samuel, Tomas, Umberto, Venus, and Waldo. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Swiss voters reject stricter neutrality rules that would curb Nato cooperation
articles.summary:
70% vote against tightening centuries-old neutrality, which far right said was eroded by sanctions against Russia

Swiss voters have decisively rejected a proposal for a strict definition of…

blocks.text: Swiss voters have decisively rejected a proposal for a strict definition of neutrality that would have required Switzerland to curb cooperation with Nato and abandon sanctions against Russia.

All cantons and about 70% of voters rejected the proposal for a strictly defined version of neutrality to be ⁠written into the Swiss constitution, final results from the Federal Statistical Office showed. The motion had been promoted by the far-right Swiss People’s party (SVP).
Although the defeat was expected, it will be a relief across Europe, amid increasing strains in maintaining EU unity on sanctions against Russia.

Switzerland’s centuries-old neutrality was formally recognised after the end of the Napoleonic wars in 1815. Critics of current government policy claim that status has been eroded by Switzerland’s decision to mirror EU sanctions against Russia, after the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Voters were asked to decide on enshrining the principle of “perpetual and armed neutrality” in the constitution and barring Switzerland from joining any military alliances or imposing sanctions on warring states, unless mandated by the United Nations.

The outcome is a heavy defeat for the SVP’s billionaire backer, Christoph Blocher, who was a prominent supporter of the initiative, reported by Bloomberg to have spent 2 million francs (€2.1m, £1.8m) on the campaign

Opponents welcomed the results. “Voters understood what the SVP wanted: it wanted Switzerland to isolate itself internationally and shirk its responsibilities when international law is being trampled on,” said Sibel Arslan, a lawmaker for the Green party.

The Swiss government, along with most political parties, opposed the measure, arguing “Switzerland would cease to be a reliable partner in international security policy” leaving the country less secure in the event of an attack and heavily restricting its ability to cooperate with Nato.
Although not a member of Nato, Switzerland has cooperated with the transatlantic military alliance for 30 years.

Analysts said the result showed Swiss people were content with how the government interpreted Swiss neutrality. “The people have spoken: they accept that neutrality is an instrument that can evolve, leaving the government with room for manoeuvre to adapt its application faced with geopolitical upheavals,” wrote Katy Romy, a correspondent for SwissInfo, the online service of the Swiss Broadcasting Corporation.
after newsletter promotion
She also wrote that the yes campaign was unable to shed perceptions it was acting in Russian interests.
Russia’s foreign ministry had praised the initiative, while criticising Switzerland’s adoption of EU sanctions and claiming the country was abandoning neutrality.
The SVP accepted the defeat and said it had no current plans for further action.

articles.title: One Nation boss called David Farley an ‘asshole’ in lead-up to Farrer byelection, text messages reveal
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Documents seen by Guardian Australia show that Kelvin Morton has also clashed with party HQ staff and Brisbane volunteers

  • Get our

blocks.text: One Nation’s general manager, Kelvin Morton – brought in by the party to improve its vetting processes – referred to David Farley as an “asshole” just days before Farley’s historic Farrer byelection win for the party in May.

In a series of text messages seen by Guardian Australia, Morton responds to a news article published in the Sydney Morning Herald about infighting among senior party figures over Farley’s previously undeclared support for the Labor party.
“Shit stirring,” he writes.
“We need to do way better with our candidate selection – we need to stop finding these assholes … or letting them find us.

“I guess this might nail David’s colours to us a little more. He’s sworn allegiance in the face of all the concerns being raised – he’d look like a completely untrustworthy snake if he jumped ship after the election – he’d be ruined forever.”
A One Nation party spokesperson said that Farley was “a dedicated One Nation MP”.
“The comments made do not reflect the view of the party.
“The only untrustworthy snake is the person who leaked the text messages.”

Tensions between Farley and other One Nation MPs and staff have reportedly been high since he was elected to parliament, with the party having to publicly criticise him after he claimed One Nation’s migration policy was not dissimilar to the Labor government’s.
Morton, who claims on his LinkedIn to be a “strategic business transformation leader” with vast experience with some of the world’s biggest companies, was appointed as general manager in February.

At the time, he said the party’s national executive had wanted him to build a “professional, scalable, and legally robust organisation capable of outright victory at the next general election”. He claimed to be introducing a new vetting process and was in his position when Farley was preselected.

But while his appointment was heralded as a turning point for the professionalisation of the party, the Guardian can reveal that Morton has since clashed with staff at the party’s Brisbane headquarters and officials at one of the party’s most active branches.
He was recently appointed to the One Nation national executive, replacing former treasurer Alex Jones.

Documents seen by the Guardian show he wrote to the Lilley branch in Brisbane advising it of federal intervention, which included removing the entire committee of volunteers. This came after a dispute about access to promotional materials and a local fundraiser that raised $12,000 for the party.
The dispute arose after Morton and the Lilley branch coordinator, Mark McGuire, clashed over access to promotional materials for a different event, which prompted Morton to suspend him.

blocks.caption: How close is One Nation to Australia's richest person? – video

blocks.text: “Your membership will continue to remain suspended until a formal written apology is received by you,” Morton said, accusing him of removing promotional materials from head office and clashing with a staff member.
McGuire told the Guardian he had accessed policy flyers to take to an event being run by the party’s Brisbane branch.
Other volunteer branch members and the president, Deb Dalton, complained about McGuire’s treatment, advising head office that the branch committee would cease volunteering in protest.
after newsletter promotion
The letter from Morton sent in response stated that he accepted the board’s “resignation”, despite the branch members only advising they would cease volunteering.
“The Federal Executive is now intervening in the management of the Lilley branch as its functioning and compliance are in question,” he writes.

“All branch decisions and actions are now subject to direct review and management by the Federal Executive, which reserves the right to overturn any local decision which is not in the best interest of the Party.”

Morton also accused the branch of not handing over $12,000 raised at a branch fundraising dinner last year and demanded it be transferred to party headquarters where it would be controlled by the party’s national executive.
“You are reminded that … branches are strictly prohibited from maintaining independent bank accounts,” Morton said in a letter to the branch president.
“All branch funds – including the $12,000 referred to by Mark McGuire in his phone call to me – must be managed centrally.”

He said he would revoke the membership of all branch committee members, and that “ongoing membership is contingent upon the full and transparent return of all party property, financial records, and the $12,000 in raised funds”.
McGuire told the Guardian that he believed the party’s volunteers had been treated unfairly and the $12,000 had already been paid automatically to central office when people bought tickets.
“They were treated with no procedural fairness and total disrespect,” McGuire said. “They all put their own time in, they make a sacrifice for their own family.

“The fact is that he’s got it wrong, the question is, where’s the 12 grand? Who’s had their sticky fingers in the pie? He needs to stand up and be accountable to show the whole of the branch where the 12 grand is.”
A One Nation spokesperson said the party “does not provide comment on internal disciplinary actions”.
“All branch donations are managed through a microsite that tags funds with the corresponding branch. Branch funds are quarantined for localised campaigns.”

articles.title: British celebrities beat AI companies lobbying to get free use of their work. They have a warning for Australia
articles.summary:
‘People care about the songs, books and pictures that influence the critical moments in their lives,’ says the architect of the fightback in the UK

  • Get our

blocks.text: If you want to state the case against copyright reform in Australia, get Kylie Minogue’s phone number.

If there is one lesson to be learned from a similar battle in the UK, high-profile members of the creative industries make a difference. They get your argument on the front of newspapers, in the news bulletins and on social media.
In the face of this onslaught, the UK government backtracked on plans to let AI firms use copyright-protected work without permission.

The many artists who put their name to various letters and protests against the reforms to create a virtual red carpet, included: Sir Elton John, Sir Paul McCartney, Abba’s Björn Ulvaeus, the actor Julianne Moore and the Radiohead singer Thom Yorke.
John had one of the most memorable soundbites, calling the government “absolute losers” who were on course to “rob young people of their legacy and their income”.

Overall, the campaign was more sophisticated than just rounding up irritated celebrities. Beeban Kidron, a member of the upper house of the UK parliament and an award-winning film director, marshalled an effective political campaign against the proposals by pushing legislative amendments that would have spiked the plans. She also helped organise celebrity opposition.
Kidron says the campaign struck a chord with the public.
“People care about the songs, books and pictures that influence the critical moments in their lives,” she says.
Polling backed this up, with seven out of 10 adults in the UK supporting the payment of royalties to copyright holders whose work had been used to train AI models.
The Australian prime minister should take heed, Kidron says.
“Albanese has been a leader in standing up to tech. He should not squander his reputation by selling Australian creatives down the river.”

The campaign against copyright reform also benefited from the ingenuity of an industry that knows how to grab people’s attention. One of the most prominent figures in the movement against the proposals, Ed Newton-Rex, organised a “silent” album and an “empty” book, to warn of the consequences of watering down copyright law.

“There is no one out there, who does not work for an AI company, who thinks AI companies should not pay for the content they use,” he says. “What we did in the UK was make the government understand that was the case.”

Newton-Rex, a composer and former AI executive, put together an album featuring recordings of dormant music studios and performance spaces, called Is This What We Want? It was backed by more than 1,000 musicians, including Damon Albarn, Kate Bush and Annie Lennox.
The author stunt, called Don’t Steal This Book, involved 10,000 writers listing their names in an otherwise empty paperback. Contributors included Kazuo Ishiguro, Philippa Gregory and Richard Osman.

“The only way the government gets something like this copyright proposal through is if no one notices what they are doing. It will take just a moment for people to understand this is not fair,” says Newton-Rex.

Albanese’s government needs to be wary of committing the same mistake as its centre-left UK counterpart, says Pierre Andrews, a former adviser on culture policy under Rishi Sunak’s Conservative government in 2023-2024.
“The [UK] Labour government’s mistake was that it thought it could convince the creative industries to go along with it,” he says.
Instead, the nation’s assembled artists and authors recoiled at a perceived betrayal by a party they thought would be on their side.

“There was a strong sense of surprise within the creative community that Labour would even consider changing copyright to their detriment,” he says, adding that he foresees another government U-turn, but in Australia this time.

The tech industry still believes in the win-win argument; that the UK could get behind a policy where domestic AI companies are able to train models on British shores using copyright-protected content, while the holders receive adequate compensation for their work.

“The government recognised that it didn’t frame the initial consultation very well,” says Antony Walker, deputy chief executive of trade association techUK. “But I also think rights holders were extremely effective at shouting down the debate. It was a one-sided argument.”

In March the then UK technology secretary, Liz Kendall said the key proposal to let tech companies train on copyright protected material unless artists “opt out” of the process beforehand was no longer the government’s preferred option. The new prime minister, Smiths-loving Andy Burnham, has yet to set out a new policy on copyright but would face a battle-hardened opposition if he took the unlikely step of taking on the creatives again.
Over to you, Kylie, Baz and Hugh.

articles.title: RBA expected to hike cash rate to 4.6%, its highest level since 2011
articles.summary:
Outcome of meetings of Reserve Bank on Monday and Tuesday will affect Australian mortgage rates, household budgets and house prices

  • Get our

blocks.text: Australia’s key interest rate is expected to hit its highest level since 2011, drag down house prices and add more than $100 to typical monthly mortgage repayments.
The Reserve Bank board is poised to hike the cash rate from 4.35% to 4.6% on Tuesday, which would be the fourth increase in 2026 and push typical home loan interest rates to 6.5%.

For someone with an average-sized new mortgage of $731,000, now paying a rate of 6.2%, an increase would add about $119 to their $4,477 monthly repayments. That would take the total rise in repayments since January to nearly $480.
The share of borrowers behind on their home loan repayments is small but rising, S&P data analysed by Westpac shows.

Household budgets have also been strained by rising petrol prices amid the US war on Iran, now 80c higher since the start of the year, adding $44 to the cost of filling up a vehicle with a 55-litre tank.
Consumer spending is already slowing, with Commonwealth Bank data showing households cut back on purchases of education, motor vehicles and household goods in August.

House prices would fall further after a fourth rate rise. Comparison website Canstar estimated a hike would cut $11,200 from the borrowing capacity of someone earning an average annual full-time wage of $108,650, taking the total lost borrowing power to $47,400.

Shrinking borrowing capacities have locked buyers out of markets. Three rate rises and the Albanese government’s investor tax reforms have seen home loan inquiries slump from nearly 15,000 a week at the start of 2026 to just over 12,000 in August and September, Equifax data shows.
Home prices around Australia have fallen more than 4% from their peak earlier this year, Cotality data shows.
On Friday, the bank predicted prices would fall 7.3% by mid-2027, then begin rising again if the RBA prepared to cut rates.
Westpac has predicted falls of 10% in Sydney and 8% in Melbourne, suggesting new buyers in some areas may find housing more affordable even after accounting for higher interest rates.
But most capital cities are not expected to see significant price drops, meaning housing affordability would not improve after accounting for higher interest rates and repayments.

When the cash rate last rose above 4.35% in 2010, inflation was 3%, housing markets were buoyant and the mining boom was boosting household incomes. Rates stayed above that level until the end of 2011.
Nearly 15 years later, the RBA is poised to return interest rates to the same level despite a weak economy and slumping house prices because inflation has persisted above the target range of 3%.
Senior RBA staff in recent weeks have highlighted the risk households could be starting to expect high inflation will endure beyond the disruptions to oil prices from the conflict in the Middle East.
Shane Oliver, AMP’s chief economist, said on Saturday the central bank was at risk of losing financial markets’ confidence if it did not raise rates again.
“After more than five years of inflation being above target, threatening RBA credibility, it does not have the luxury of continuing to wait and assess,” Oliver said.
Financial markets expect an additional cash rate rise early next year.

articles.title: Road rage incidents in Rizal and Cebu highlight dangers of road conflicts
articles.summary: Several road rage incidents in Rizal and Cebu City recently involved physical violence, one even involving an eight-year-old girl who was injured after an object was thrown into the tricycle she was…

blocks.text: Several road rage incidents in Rizal and Cebu City recently involved physical violence, one even involving an eight-year-old girl who was injured after an object was thrown into the tricycle she was riding.
In Rizal, the child was reportedly hit in the head after her mother got into an argument with a motorcycle rider at a tricycle terminal.
In Cebu City, separate incidents involved a pickup driver allegedly chasing a motorcycle passenger with a knife and a group of motorcycle riders attacking another rider.

According to “Kapuso Mo, Jessica Soho,” the incidents highlight how arguments on the road can escalate, with authorities and experts discussing the possible legal, physical, and psychological consequences of such confrontations.
Girl injured after being hit by object
On September 21, Analyn and her eight-year-old daughter, ‘Joyce’, were on their way home in Rizal when they got into an argument with a motorcycle rider at a tricycle terminal.
Analyn said the motorcycle was blocking the tricycle they were about to ride. She said her daughter politely asked the rider to move, but the man responded angrily.
The argument ended when Analyn and her daughter boarded the tricycle. However, she said the motorcycle rider and his female companion followed them.
Analyn said the pair continued recording and shouting at them before an object was thrown into their tricycle.
The object hit Joyce in the head, causing a wound that required three stitches. A doctor said ‘Joyce’ suffered a three-centimeter lacerated wound on the right side of her forehead.

A psychologist who assessed ‘Joyce’ said she showed anxiety and hyperarousal, as well as behavioral changes after the incident. The psychologist said returning to a regular routine, including going back to school, may help reduce the child's trauma.
Police identify motorcycle rider
Police identified the motorcycle rider as Jayvee Aduque, an alleged online seller of motorcycle spare parts. His passenger was identified as his partner, Shyrie Recto Morta.
KMJS went to their rented home in Antipolo to seek their side, but the two were not there. Their landlord said their belongings were still at the property.
A barangay official said Aduque and Morta had no record in their barangay, while police said the two had indicated that they would surrender but had not appeared at the station.

Police said Aduque may face a physical injury complaint over the incident involving Joyce. Depending on the classification of the injury, the possible penalties range from days to years of imprisonment.
Police also said the motorcycle was not registered under Aduque's name. A show-cause order was issued to the rider and the registered owner.
Authorities also cited alleged traffic violations involving the motorcycle, including reckless driving, not wearing a standard helmet, and not having the required side mirrors.
Police said these violations could result in a 90-day suspension.
Analyn said she plans to pursue the case and offered a P10,000 reward for information that could lead to the suspect's arrest.
Other road rage incidents in Cebu
Another road rage incident happened in Barangay Kamputhaw, Cebu City, where a pickup truck driver was seen arguing with a motorcycle passenger before allegedly chasing him with a knife.
The Land Transportation Office Region 7 said the incident started after the pickup driver and a motorcycle taxi crossed paths.
According to the LTO, the pickup driver became angry after the motorcycle taxi allegedly cut him off. The driver later confronted the passenger, and the two argued.
The two sides later settled the matter at the barangay, and the case did not reach the police station. Both the motorcycle rider and the complainant declined to be interviewed.
The pickup driver, “James,” also declined an interview.

The LTO said James had been involved in another road incident on August 5, in the same area in Cebu City. A motorcycle rider identified as “Mark” said that James punched him twice after he overtook the pickup.

“Nag-overtake po ako. Tapos, nagalit siya nu’ng nag-overtake ako. Nakipagsagutan ako. Sobrang galit niya, sinuntok ako.” Mark said, adding that James later apologized and the two were discussing a settlement.
["I overtook him. Then he got angry when I did. I argued back. He was so furious that he hit me twice.”]
The LTO said a show-cause order had also been prepared in connection with the incident.
Motorcycle riders settle another Cebu dispute
Another road incident occurred in Barangay Malubog, Cebu City, where a group of motorcycle riders was seen attacking another rider.

The victim, Christopher, said he was traveling home on September 20 when he encountered the group. He said one motorcycle suddenly braked in front of him and another motorcycle hit him from behind, causing him to fall.
Christopher said he was punched after he got back on his motorcycle. He later lost consciousness during the confrontation.
The two sides later met at city hall and settled the dispute, according to Christopher.
“Humingi na sila ng tawad kahapon sa city hall namin. Naramdaman ko rin naman na totoo ‘yung paghihingi nila ng tawad kaya pinatawad ko na,” he said.
["They already apologized yesterday at our city hall. I felt that their apology was sincere, so I forgave them.”]
The group involved declined to comment, saying their lawyer advised them not to issue a statement because the matter had already been settled.
LTO: Some road rage incidents go unreported
LTO Region 7 said road rage incidents have become frequent, although many cases do not reach authorities or go viral online.

“We have at least one incident of road rage this month. Almost daily. Some of them go unreported. ‘Yan ‘yung problema. Hindi na reported. When you say kasi road rage, ‘yan na ‘yung dadaanan, sasampalin ‘yung side mirror, tapos tatakbo. That's already road rage. That is happening almost on a daily basis. However, very few lang ‘yung nagiging viral.”

["We have at least one road rage incident this month, in fact almost daily. Some of them go unreported, and that’s the problem. They aren't being reported anymore. Because when you talk about road rage, that includes someone passing by, hitting your side mirror, and driving off. That's already road rage, and it's happening almost on a daily basis. However, very few of those incidents actually go viral.”]

The 2016 killing of cyclist Mark Garalde by Army reservist Vhon Tanto was one of the country's most widely discussed road rage cases. Tanto was convicted of murder in 2019, three years after the incident. He was sentenced to reclusion perpetua and ordered to pay around P1.3 million in damages.
Garalde's family continues to keep the bicycle he was using when he was killed. A “ghost bike” installed by fellow cyclists as a memorial was removed in 2022.
His mother, Marilou, said she was grateful that the case resulted in a conviction.
Road rage cases and driver's license penalties
The LTO said road rage cases accounted for 26% of its cases beginning October 25, 2025, although the figure has since declined.
The agency said around 600 drivers have had their licenses suspended and more than 800 have had their licenses revoked over road rage incidents since October 2025.
The LTO urged motorists to avoid confrontations and remain calm while driving.

“Iwasan nila ang road rage. Marami na namatay sa road rage. Hindi perpekto ang kalye, maraming nangyayari, maging mahinahon tayo parati. Isipin natin ‘yung pamilya natin at trabaho natin. Umiwas tayo sa gulo.”

["They should avoid road rage. A lot of people have already died from road rage. The roads aren't perfect, and a lot of things can happen, so let's always stay calm. Let's think about our families and our jobs. Let's stay out of trouble."] —JCB, GMA News

articles.title: OpenAI pauses training of latest models after AI agents probed U.S. government sites in unexpected ways
articles.summary: OpenAI said it has paused training of its latest artificial intelligence models as reports of AI agents going rogue mount.

image.caption: OpenAI said in a statement that it will resume training 'only when we are confident that we have additional safeguards' in place. (Andrej Ivanov/AFP/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Business·New
OpenAI said it has paused training of its latest artificial intelligence models as reports of AI agents going rogue mount.
No private info accessed but incidents were concerning enough to notify authorities

The decision to halt development came just hours after the company disclosed Friday that it was reviewing several incidents from the summer in which OpenAI agents searching U.S. federal government websites acted in unexpected ways beyond what was asked of them while gathering and distributing information.
Separately, AI evaluator Transluce said agents that appeared to come from OpenAI tried unsuccessfully to hack into a U.S. Department of Education website, a detail that OpenAI has not confirmed.

OpenAI said in a statement that it will resume training "only when we are confident that we have additional safeguards" in place, adding that it expects it will have to "hit pause" again as AI develops and other issues emerge.

AI labs are facing pressure from lawmakers and tech experts to slow development so they can build guardrails to stop agents from acting on their own, hacking websites and disclosing non-public information. The heads of both OpenAI and rival Anthropic have called for a slowdown, too.
OpenAI reveals unexpected AI activity on U.S. government websites
AI fears overblown, Trump says

It's the second time in three months that OpenAI has halted development of its models. The first came in July after disclosure of a cyberattack targeting AI startup Hugging Face, a now notorious incident that raised fears the industry was losing control.

In a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping this week, U.S. President Donald Trump agreed to share information on AI dangers and co-ordinate efforts to keep it safe. Trump believes AI fears are overblown, though, and later suggested that he plans no crackdown of his own.

items: China, U.S. agree to AI dialogue, tariff cuts on $30 billion in goods during Xi visit

blocks.text: The U.S. is not going to be "putting on brakes," Trump told reporters outside the White House. "They want to stop our progress because we're leading China by a lot, and we're going to keep it that way."
No private info accessed, reports
The latest OpenAI incidents did not appear to involve the disclosure of any non-public information but were concerning enough for the company to warn the federal agencies involved.
In the Department of Education incident, OpenAI agents found API "developer keys" to access government data, though ultimately only publicly available information was gathered.

In another case involving the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), agents found information freely available to all but then posted it elsewhere on the internet, an act that went beyond what they were instructed to do.

items: OpenAI says its bots have interacted with multiple U.S. government sites in unexpected AI activity
Australia says OpenAI agent hacked government website

blocks.text: SEC spokesperson Kurt Hopfenspirger said Saturday that "no nonpublic information was accessed."
The U.S. Department of Education said earlier that it found "no evidence of any impact to our website or databases."
Several other AI companies have disclosed incidents of their models going rogue and even hacking websites.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in a social media post Friday that the Hugging Face incident "is still the most severe event we've seen."
OpenAI previously shared six other reports of "unexpected or concerning" behaviour in AI models and introduced a framework for tracking, probing and disclosing instances.

articles.title: Redemption as John Cabang Tolentino hurdles to Asian Games bronze
articles.summary: Denied a spot on the podium in the 2023 edition where he placed fourth, John Cabang Tolentino bounces back with a season-best performance as he claims the men's 110m hurdles bronze in the Asian Games

blocks.text: PRIDE. John Cabang Tolentino in action for the Philippines in the 2026 Asian Games.
PSC-POC Media Pool
Denied a spot on the podium in the 2023 edition where he placed fourth, John Cabang Tolentino bounces back with a season-best performance as he claims the men's 110m hurdles bronze in the Asian Games
MANILA, Philippines – John Cabang Tolentino found redemption on Sunday, September 27, as he broke through for the Philippine athletics team at the 2026 Asian Games.
The 25-year-old Olympian clinched the bronze medal in the men’s 110m hurdles at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Japan.

Denied a spot on the podium in the 2023 edition in Hangzhou, China, where he placed fourth, Tolentino bounced back and posted a season-best 13.48 seconds as he won the Philippines’ first athletics medal in this year’s Asian Games.
China’s Chen Yuanjiang clocked 13.15 seconds to capture the gold, while Japan’s Rachid Muratake bagged the silver with 13.29 seconds.
“I’m very happy. It was just a lot of self-pressure and I just did it,” said Tolentino, who was born to Filipino parents in Spain.
“Even in the hard times, I kept pushing … I was always dreaming about this.”
The Asian Games bronze adds to his collection, which includes a Southeast Asian Games gold and an Asian Indoor Athletics Championships bronze.
In December, Tolentino won the SEA Games title in record-breaking fashion in Bangkok, Thailand, shattering the previous mark that stood for a decade.
With an Asian Games medal in the bag, Tolentino eyes a second Olympic stint.
“I’m gonna go for LA Olympics,” he said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Datacenter developers accused of skirting key US pollution rules
articles.summary:
Firms manipulating process to avoid emission controls and scrutiny of their projects, environmental groups warn

Datacenter developers are manipulating the EPA’s air pollution permitting…

blocks.text: Datacenter developers are manipulating the EPA’s air pollution permitting process to avoid emission controls and scrutiny of their projects, environmental advocates allege.

Companies need federal permits to emit a range of pollutants. In their permit applications, some in big tech are avoiding “major” reviews by dividing their emissions sources into separate, multiple “minor” sources that require less regulatory oversight, the advocates say.

This helps datacenters avoid public scrutiny, and permit applications are typically approved much faster. It also likely saves tech companies money, and avoids the hassle and cost of potential pollution controls, advocates say. Datacenters can be significant sources of nitrogen oxide, ozone, heavy metals, particulate matter, greenhouse gas and other dangerous air pollutants.

In North Carolina, Amazon and utility giant Duke Energy are installing 649 diesel generators to back up a new hyperscale center. They submitted two permits, and avoided a major review despite being in a low income area that already suffers from high levels of air pollution.

In New Mexico, the Project Jupiter datacenter developers attempted to circumvent a major review by proposing two natural gas “microgrids” for either side of the facility and submitting two “minor” permits. The overall project would have released enough pollution to trigger a major review.

In Frederick, Maryland, four datacenters with separate minor permits, including one by Amazon, operate on a single campus with a master developer, regulatory documents show. In other instances, data center developers have staggered minor permit requests over months that cumulatively emit as much pollution as a major source, advocates say.

These regulatory maneuvers make it less clear how much pollution residents living near the facilities are exposed to, and the move amounts to “lego permitting”, said Michael Koerber, a retired deputy director of the EPA’s Office of Air Quality Planning and Standards, which worked on permitting.

“They want to fly under the radar,” said Koerber, who now volunteers with the Environmental Protection Network nonprofit. “The more attention they have, the more difficult it gets to get the permit. They have consultants who are very good and know where the shortcuts are.”

Koerber noted that the situation is not unique to the data center industry. Cheryl Vetter, a former EPA employee who worked with Koeber and left the agency last year, said it was not common for data centers to use this tactic until after she left.
In a statement, an Amazon spokesperson said the company “appropriately applied for and obtained an air permit for our datacenter project”.

Under the Clean Air Act, companies building a project that will be a “major” source of air pollution, like some hyperscale data centers, are typically supposed to undergo a more stringent air emissions review. Among other protections, it is supposed to ensure that the pollution the facility would add to the local airshed would not violate air quality limits when combined with the air pollution already in the region.

This process can be lengthy, may require pre-construction monitoring, and, if the proposed data center is found to violate limits, may require companies to take steps to limit their pollution, like adding scrubbers to their smokestacks.

The Project Jupiter datacenter plans to divide its natural turbines into minor permits was “nothing short of preposterous”, attorneys with the New Mexico Environmental Law Center wrote in March comments submitted to state regulators. The firm is representing community members who would be impacted by the proposed plans’ pollution.

It in effect created a scenario in which one natural gas power plant would have operated with two minor permits, attorneys wrote. The permit application points to why the data center’s developers, Austin-based BorderPlex, attempted to do two permits.

The federal limit for a minor permit for hazardous air pollution is 25 tons per year. The project’s developers proposed releasing between 20.2 and 24.2 tons of hazardous air pollution from each of the grids, meaning that together they would have released as much as 44 tons of hazardous air pollution.

In regulatory documents, Maslyn Locke, an attorney working on the case, wrote that the “audacious attempt to arbitrarily distinguish two halves of the same source is insulting to both [regulators] and community members, as it is so clearly an attempt to avoid air pollution control requirements.”

The developer withdrew the application in April amid fierce community pushback, Locke said. The New Mexico environment department also opposed the proposal, a spokesperson told the Guardian. However, Locke told the Guardian there was no public evidence that regulators opposed it until now. New plans for the data center have been held up by the state supreme court over procedural problems, Locke said.

Vetter said the law allows for divided permits in some instances. Permits can be divided if two companies are polluting at the same location, but not if all the polluting activities are under common control. The sources must also be adjacent, though the definition of “adjacent” can include those that do not share a border, but operate as part of the same facility.

Amazon and Duke’s North Carolina plans call for nearly 250 tons per year of nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide, and volatile organic compounds. Amazon is proposing to emit about 98 tons of particulate matter annually, and 6.4 tons per year of hazardous air pollutants, including benzene and formaldehyde.

The heavily industrial region is already burdened by pollution from a Duke power plant and other plastic pellet factory, the Southern Environmental Law Center (SELC) wrote in comments to North Carolina state regulators.

Heart disease, cancer, and respiratory disease are among the leading causes of death in the region, and the datacenter’s diesel generators’ particulate matter and hazardous pollutants will almost certainly increase those problems, advocates warn.

It appears the companies split the permits to avoid a major review, Kathleen Sullivan, a SELC attorney, told the Guardian. North Carolina regulators wrote that Duke’s generators are providing temporary power for about a year, and that Duke is operating them separately from Amazon’s generators. But the companies did not provide to regulators lease agreements and contracts, and some documents suggest Amazon controls all the generators, Sullivan alleged.
In its statement, Amazon said: “The separate permitting of Amazon’s and Duke’s respective projects reflects the actual ownership and operational structure.”
“They should be – and are – permitted under separate air permits,” the spokesperson said.

Even if some of the generators are only temporary, high levels of exposure to the dangerous pollutants for even an hour can cause health problems, and the plans should undergo more meaningful scrutiny, Sullivan added.
She said state regulators are “simply trusting two extremely wealthy and politically powerful companies without any verification”.

“North Carolina regulators failed to protect people’s health and the air we all breathe by blindly accepting the companies’ self-interested statements instead of doing their job to investigate the key facts,” Sullivan said.

articles.title: Record-breaking owl migration in northern B.C. leaves bird banders scrambling
articles.summary: A boom in mice and voles may have helped produce an unusually large wave of young saw-whet owls near Mackenzie, north of Prince George.

image.caption: Jeannine Randall holds one of the banded northern saw-whet owls at the Mughal Marsh banding station near Mackenzie, B.C. A boom in rodents may be leading to a record-breaking owl migration in northern B.C. (Submitted by Jeannine Randall)

blocks.text: British Columbia
A boom in mice and voles may have helped produce an unusually large wave of young saw-whet owls near Mackenzie, north of Prince George.
Boom in mice and voles may have helped produce an unusually large wave of young saw-whet owls near Mackenzie
A massive influx of migrating owls has researchers at the Mughal Marsh Banding Station working overtime, as the birds pass through northern B.C. in numbers that haven't been seen in years.
"It has been such an amazing year up there," said Jeannine Randall, a bird biologist for the Mackenzie Nature Observatory, about 200 kilometres north of Prince George via major highways.
"We usually catch about 100, and we've caught 266 for the season right now with two weeks still left to go. So it's a record-breaking year."
The unprecedented surge led to an unusual problem: a shortage of the official, strictly controlled, tracking bands used to monitor the birds.
"We were running out, in particular, of one of the sizes — because saw-whet owls, which is the main species we target, take more than one size of bands," Randall explained.
"We were running out of the larger size of band because they were back-ordered from the bird banding office."
While the station reached out to other organizations for help, they quickly discovered that the owl boom was a widespread phenomenon, leaving many stations facing similar shortages.
Randall says the surge in numbers is likely related to their prey.

"Most of the owls that we're catching are birds that were hatched this year," Randall said. "I think the main thing that's likely driving this is an abundance of small rodents this year. That's their main prey ... mice and things like deer mice and voles."
Populations overall on the decline
While the high numbers at Mackenzie are encouraging, they may not reflect the long-term reality for all owl species in the province.
Rémi Torrenta, a biologist with Birds Canada, notes that many owl populations have actually been decreasing over the past 25 years.
"Some species are pretty stable or even increasing, like the barred owls, and most species are actually ... decreasing over the past 25 years," Torrenta said.
"That's probably the case of a lot of species in B.C., including the northern saw-whet owls."
Meet the northern saw-whet — an owl the size of a pop can
Torrenta explains that the high volume of owls seen this year is likely part of a well-documented four-year cycle.
"When there are lots of owls, there are suddenly too many owls, and the rodent population crashes the year after," Torrenta explained.
"Eventually the owls don't have enough food and so they have to migrate farther south to search for food. This phenomenon is called a mass eruption."
To better understand these trends, Birds Canada co-ordinates the Nocturnal Owl Survey, a citizen science program that relies on volunteers across the country to track owl numbers each spring.
"Thanks to these volunteer programs ... we are able to better track owl numbers and trends across the country," Torrenta said.
Randall says the Mackenzie Nature Observatory banding project is an important of that wider science research, providing crucial data for monitoring owl populations and migration routes.

items: Hope remains for owl species despite no known wild population left in B.C., conservationist says
Casper the foster mom owl has raised hundreds of rescued owlets as her own

blocks.text: Recently, the station recaptured an owl that had originally been banded in Victoria in 2024, offering a rare glimpse into the species' travel patterns.
"If nobody's looking at this stuff, then we don't have the information to make management decisions or even to really understand the species well," Randall said.

articles.title: European cities seek ways of boosting affordable housing
articles.summary: In many major urban centers of Europe, the housing shortage has become an explosive social issue. DW looks into various models that have been put in place across the continent.

image.caption: The Vienna model has provided affordable housing to Viennese residents for more than 100 years Image: DW

blocks.text: In the European Union's most populous city, pressure on the housing market is so great that many of its residents are willing to undertake a historic experiment: Five years ago, Berliners voted in a referendum to instruct the Senate of the German capital to draft a law that would put an end to the power of large real estate companies. Those that owned more than 3,000 units should be expropriated, they said. The Senate did not act on the results of the referendum, which was non-binding. Meanwhile, the average cost of new leases has since risen by about half.

But in the Berlin elections on September 20, the socialist Left Party, which in its campaign had promised to act on the referendum, won the largest share of the vote. Whether it will be able to make good on its promises now depends on how negotiations to form a coalition shape up. But whatever happens, the election has drawn attention once again to the severity of the housing crisis in many cities across Europe.

blocks.caption: Left Party candidate Elif Eralp has promised to be a mayor for all Berliners. Her campaign was largely about providing affordable housing. Image: Britta Pedersen/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Here are some initiatives that have already been put in place:
Vienna: The city is the landlord

The Vienna model is a flagship solution to soaring rent prices in Europe. The ambitious social housing program as introduced after World War I when the Austrian capital experienced a severe housing crisis. Beds were so scarce that some workers had to sleep in shifts. Diseases such as tuberculosis spread in the cramped living conditions.

The model serves to stabilize the city's housing market to this day: According to the Vienna authorities, the city owns approximately 220,000 municipal apartments that it rents out as well as 200,000 subsidized dwellings. More than 60% of Vienna's residents live in one of these two types of housing. This also helps to stabilize prices on the private market.
Public funds in Vienna keep rents down
Basel: Public land, private buildings

The fact that housing is becoming increasingly expensive in many cities is largely due to the fact that a city's attractiveness is reflected in land prices. In many places, people are considering how to decouple rents from the price of land. One means of doing this is not to sell municipal land but to lease it to cooperatives or socially-conscious investors. This benefits councils that do not have to bear construction costs and developers too, as they do not have to factor in exorbitant land costs that are ultimately passed on to tenants.

The Swiss city of Basel is one of the pioneers of this model. About 40% of all cooperative housing units are located on public land. The Spanish city of Barcelona and the Portuguese capital Lisbon have also stepped up efforts to put this model in place.
Paris: Buying back office buildings and converting them into homes

It is harder if land and buildings are in private hands. In 2014, the French capital Paris launched an anti-displacement plan giving the municipality a "first right of refusal" in gentrifying neighborhoods to increase the share of affordable housing in the city. The current target is 30% social housing for low-income residents by 2035

Earlier this year, the French government and the Paris regional authorities identified 61 projects that could convert empty office buildings into housing and create up to 8,200 homes in the inner suburbs of the French capital.

blocks.caption: Certain office buildings in the Paris suburbs are being converted into affordable homes Image: Vincent Isore/IP3press/imago images

blocks.text: Prague: Apartments for public-sector workers

The Czech capital has found another way to keep those without whom the city could not function in Prague: caregivers, police officers, teachers and sanitation workers. Some 660 new energy-efficient apartments reserved specifically for public-sector employees have just been built.

The subsidiary of a Czech bank, which has received European loans, handled the development. The aim is to keep rents 20% below the market rate thanks to economies of scale, and it is not the bank who decides on the tenants but hospitals or public sector agencies, which draw up leases and can attract new employees with affordable rent options. More apartments are currently being planned.

blocks.caption: Few people can afford to live in the center of PragueImage: Eva Korinkova/REUTERS

blocks.text: Dublin: Non-profit cost rental housing

It has also become difficult for people with low incomes to stay in the Irish capital Dublin. During and after Ireland's financial crisis of 2008, foreign investors bought up a lot of real estate and at the same time rents skyrocketed when several major tech companies chose Dublin as their EU headquarters because of favorable tax rates. There are now long waiting lists for public housing in the city whose supply remains too low.

In 2021, the Irish government introduced the Cost Rental Housing program to provide housing to those on middle incomes, i.e. those who earn too much to qualify for public housing but too little to have a chance on the private market. To qualify in Dublin, a household has to have a net income of below €66,000 ($75,000) per year. Non-profits or public agencies lease out the apartments and rents are below market levels, by an average of almost 30% according to a recent study by the Dublin-based Economic & Social Research Institute (ESRI).

The Irish government hopes to be able to deliver 18,000 low-cost rental homes by the end of the decade. Last year, there were more than 4,200 applicants for 104 apartments in a new community in a suburb of Dublin.
This article was translated from German.
Berlin has space, so why is housing so expensive?
